owner: Executive director, until the board names an owner
why: We want AI to take routine writing off our plate. We must protect SNAP applicants, donors and volunteers, and keep a real person for anyone who needs help.
who_it_covers: Staff, contractors and board members. Whether volunteers may use AI is still open for the board.

tools.name: Gemini (in Google Workspace)
tools.approved_for: Drafting and editing only; no protected information.

new_tools: Ken (IT) approves new tools, plugins, AI agents and AI features in existing software, after checking what data they see and whether the vendor trains on it.
accounts: Use your work Google account and turn off vendor training on what you type.
everyone_now: Staff may use Gemini in a work account for work with no information about a real person. Volunteer use waits for the board's decision.
allowed_uses: Write general volunteer thank-yous; add names yourself afterward.
Draft grant boilerplate about our work.

needs_approval.use: Donor information in an AI tool
Reports to funders or Feeding America
Anything using a corporate partner's logo or brand

protected_information: SNAP applicants' Social Security numbers, income, household members and immigration documents (state human services agreement); donor names and giving records in Salesforce; volunteer names, phone numbers, emergency contacts and court-ordered case details; mobile pantry sign-up names and zip codes; passwords and logins.
off_limits: No SNAP application information goes into any AI tool.
No AI answers SNAP eligibility questions. A person answers the SNAP line.
No AI images of hungry people. Our photos are real, with consent forms.
check_before_it_goes_out: Whoever sends AI-assisted work owns it. Check facts, names, numbers and tone first.
Pounds and people served come from the inventory system, never an AI draft.
Check recall and allergen details against the original notice.
decisions_about_people: AI never decides who gets help, benefits or a volunteer role. Trained people decide.
being_open: We follow the AI clause in our corporate partner's agreement.
If a funder or partner asks about our AI use, we answer honestly.
if_something_goes_wrong: Tell your manager and Ken the same day. Reporting a mistake is expected, never punished.
who_owns_this: The executive director owns this policy until the board names someone; Ken approves tools.
The board's executive committee approves changes. We review it in 12 months.
open_questions: Do we approve or stop staff's personal ChatGPT and Claude use, and will we pay for any AI accounts next year?
Should AI reminder texts in the volunteer scheduling software stay on, and do we tell people when AI helped write what they get?
May volunteers, such as group leaders writing shift notes, use AI?
